4.why: Source only says stay off the dirty feature on the right; which feature the ledge tops is ambiguous

6.why: Source pitch 6: crack, overlaps, then a path through the bushes to the anchor at the end
6.text: Anchor above the second overlap, reached by a path straight up through the bushes.

8.why: Source pitch 8: friction slab ends at a hole in the rock taking gear for the belay
8.text: Gear belay in a hole in the rock that accepts pieces from one to three inches.

10.why: Source pitch 10: smearing past bolts and corner to an anchor on top of a pedestal
10.text: Anchor on top of a pedestal, above the left-facing corner.

11.why: Source pitch 11: ramp beside the dihedral, then onto the buttress crest to a chain anchor
11.text: Chain anchor on the buttress crest, above the ramp beside the Inverted Prow dihedral.

12.why: Source pitch 12: ledgy climbing up the right side of the crest to an anchor on the crest
12.text: Anchor on the crest of the buttress, up its right side.

13.why: Source pitch 13: dihedral on slab layer under the trees to an anchor on a small stance
13.text: Anchor on a small stance at the top of the slab-layer dihedral under the trees.

14.why: Source pitch 14 ends at the summit chain anchor, passing left of a tree with an old sling; 'beyond' corrected
14.text: Chain anchor at the summit, reached by passing left of the tree with the old sling.

5.why: Source numbers 11 pitches not 14; the two-pin anchor below the corner is mid-pitch (pitch continues by crack to a large ledge), so pitch end unclear

7.why: Source pitch 4 (stored 7 by notes): corners up and right to a sloping ledge with loose blocks, two-pin anchor; pitch end
7.text: Sloping ledge with loose blocks, anchored on two pins.

10.why: Source pitch 6 (stored 10 by notes): zigzag through lichen ledges about 100 ft to a ledge with a small horn and cord
10.text: Small horn on a ledge, slung with cord, past the lichen-covered ledge systems.
